To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of an external memory index structure can significantly improve the search performance of WSDs; and 2) the use of flash memory can be exploited to improve the search performance and energy efficiency of external memory index structures.

(1) the MicroHash and MicroGf index structures offer excellent performance for equality searches and spatial searches in WSDs, (2) the MicroHash index structure offers the best performance among the three structures we implemented, and (3) the cost of maintaining the MicroHash index is low.

(i) MicroGF is the first index structure for flash-based sensor nodes that supports spatial searches, and (ii) MicroHash is the first index that supports equality searches by value and by timestamp on flash-based sensor nodes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of index structures that are well suited to the specific requirements of WSDs.
the design of efficient indexing data structures for the retrieval of data stored on the local storage of WSDs.
efficient indexing and searching on flash-based sensor devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the index structures we present here are the first to offer efficient and reliable indexing capabilities to flash-based WSDs.
MicroHash and Micro GF are the best index structures for flash-based WSDs.
our index structures are very promising for WSDs that need to perform equality and spatial searches in the presence of limited energy resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our index structures are the first to offer efficient indexing and searching capabilities for the flash-based WSDs.
our index structures are well-suited for applications that require high-performance search capabilities on the flash media of WSDs.
we have developed two external memory index data structures that can be used on flash-based WSDs to enable efficient retrieval of data records.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of flash memory on WSDs does not imply a trade-off between the energy efficiency of the device and its indexing performance.
flash-based WSDs can be equipped with a rich set of indexing and search capabilities without compromising their energy budget.

the design of external index structures for the flash-based storage of sensor devices is a challenging task, which requires the exploitation of the asymmetric read/write characteristics of flash memory and the careful design of data structures and algorithms.
